title: How often swapping the individual-data trial reverses a MAIC
question: When two sponsors run MAIC on the same two trials, each weighting its own data to the other trial, how often do their conclusions reverse, how much of that is a real difference in target population rather than sampling error or differing adjustment sets, and which common-target remedy recovers the decision population's effect?
design: Two trials with linear effect modification of one treatment, 108 cells crossing population separation, modification strength, position of the zero-effect point, trial sizes and adjustment sets, plus controls; two sponsor MAICs, transport of both to a declared population, and their average. 1000 replicates per cell.
